reply_text:
Checking the real state before answering: the Zai re-dispatch was due at 22:41Z, which is several hours ago now.㊥ ("is this still going well?") Mostly yes, with one slip of mine to own. The record side is done: every hole the -40 spec needed from 象 is built and live in the running service, and the move-grammar campaign's first batch (158 turns, 782 labelled incidences) is in and analysed. The slip: five Zai seats labelling at once exhausted the five-hour token window at 18:21Z, and the timed wake I set for the reset at 22:41Z never fired, so six hours of a clear window went unused. I found that just now on your question. Batch 2 shards 1 and 2 are running again as of 04:40Z (zai-1 `invoke`… jobs parked, shards 3 to 5 follow when those finish); the monthly meter is at 56%, resetting in 21 hours, so the remaining ~200 records fit.

㊢ (what landed since you said "application led")
- Acts, standings, obligations, a typed ports status with a rules version, and the reply's own time are stored on every turn record. claude-15's follower reads them instead of running 象 code, so the spec's no-recomputation rule now holds on every seam.
- Session end is observable: the registry writes a durable outbox line on reset, deregister, reap or replaced id; the turn service turns it into a system record that lapses the agent's ports and marks yours orphaned or unread with the reason. Live since this evening; no session has ended yet, so the first such record is still to be seen.
- Tests caught one hazard: test suites had written nine fake session ends to the live outbox before the path was isolated; quarantined, fixed, never consumed.

㊬ (what the labelled data says about the kernel) Against the labellers, the kernel's links are 86% right as pairs but reach only 12% of the closes a reader sees. The candidate rule "only opener of its kind" would reach a third of the rest at 33% precision, so it is held. The current sole-port rule over-links asides 30% of the time, and every one of the 18 effect disagreements runs the same way: the kernel closes where a reader keeps. Batch 2 is the dataset to pick a tighter sole-port variant.

🈸 (one list still waiting on you, from the label consolidation) Proposals leaked into topics ("cheat-sheet", "bidding"), so for `propose` I recommend two cue-word moves, `tentative` ("I wonder if") and `directive` ("let's"), and no to the five topic labels; for `explain`, yes to `analogy`, `decision-rationale`, `consequence` and `mechanics` as an alias, no to `system-integration`. Yes or no per item, whenever.

㊟ (nothing else needs you) Three small follow-ups are noted, not dispatched: an overlapping-turn edge in the reply-time window, the first real session-end record to verify, and the hyperedge loader once the vocabulary is closed.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("we would need hypergraphs") Agreed, and the store we already have is one: futon1b's memory edges are hyperedges, and the two things the move mining produces, an answer incidence and a scope, are hyperedges by nature, one paragraph bearing on several openers, one opener governing many later acts. I want to check what the futon6 scopes actually are before I say how close the analogy is.㊢ (recorded) Your remark is in the mission beside the first one (7bf772d0), with the consequence it has for the campaign now running.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("we would need hypergraphs") Yes, and the two things the Zai mining produces are hyperedges by nature. An answer incidence is one reply paragraph bearing on several openers; a scope is one opener governing many later acts. Neither fits a binary edge, and both fit futon1b's hyperedge shape, which minus40 already uses for memory assertions and links. So the sidecars from the pilot are the mining output, not the carrier. The carrier is a `:xiang/answers` hyperedge over a paragraph and its openers, and a `:xiang/scope` hyperedge over an opener and what it governs, in the same store as the memories. That is what lets a resume brief traverse turns and memories as one graph.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (futon6 scopes, checked) Two things there, and they are both the right analogy. The thread hypergraph assembler types its nodes as post, term, expression and scope, and its hyperedges as mention, discourse, scope and so on, which is the same move: scope is a node kind with edges to what it governs. The LaTeX environment detector emits scope hyperedges from real structure, with a canonical kind table and an alias table, rather than matching prose headers, and it names the mistake that forced that: fake environments from bare "Lemma" lines. The dialogue equivalent is exactly what the pilot's validator enforces, a scope only where a verbatim act opens it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("closer to intents than memories") Agreed, and that settles where scopes live: on the 象 side, as acts' reach, in the kernel's vocabulary, not as facts in the memory store. A constraint in force, a focus declared, a mission named: each is an act whose scope is the set of later acts read under it. The kernel's standings are already half of this, the "in force until withdrawn" half; what they lack is the "governs these acts" relation, which is the hyperedge.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("that was a one off") The earlier round mined operator turns into the 26 象 patterns and stopped. The difference this time is the output target: not patterns alone but a labelled grammar that a fast tier can apply to every settled turn afterwards, classical where the grammar is regular enough, Kimi where it is not. The Zai budget pays for the mining once; the standing cost is the fast tier. The pilot's numbers on precision and cost per record are what decide whether that is realistic, and they arrive on the next wake.
